note.explanation: Chemistry studies substances: what they are made of, how their atoms are arranged, what properties they have, and how they change. Its branches let scientists focus on particular kinds of substances or questions.
examples: Finding the concentration of a substance in a sample is studied in analytical chemistry.
Studying reactions in an atom’s nucleus is studied in nuclear chemistry.
note.simple: Chemistry is the study of substances and how they behave or change.
note.checkQuestion: Which branch studies the analysis and concentration of components in a sample?
note.title: Chemistry and its branches
steps: Identify the main subject of the question, such as composition, reaction rate, or a living process.
Match that subject to the branch that studies it.
For a reaction in an atom’s nucleus, choose nuclear chemistry.
note.answer: Chemistry studies the properties, composition and structure of substances, their changes, and the principles governing those changes.

mcqs.stem: A scientist separates the components of a sample and measures their concentrations. Which branch is most directly involved?
rationales: Correct: analytical chemistry involves separation, identification and determination of component concentrations.
Biochemistry focuses on chemical substances and processes in living organisms.
Geochemistry studies the chemical composition of Earth, its sources and minerals.
Polymer chemistry focuses on the structure, properties and synthesis of polymers.

mcqs.stem: Which branch studies changes taking place in the nucleus of an atom?
rationales: Correct: nuclear chemistry deals with reactions and transformations in atomic nuclei.
Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, with certain simple carbon salts excluded.
Environmental chemistry studies chemical and biochemical phenomena in the planet’s air, soil and water.
Physical chemistry investigates how substances behave at atomic and molecular levels and how physical laws affect them.

mcqs.stem: A chemist designs and synthesizes a new drug. Which branch is the best match?
rationales: Correct: medicinal chemistry includes designing and synthesizing medicines or drugs.
Inorganic chemistry studies the synthesis, composition, properties and structure of elements and compounds containing little or no carbon.
Astrochemistry studies molecules and ions in space and interstellar space.
Polymer chemistry focuses on polymers and macromolecules.

mcqs.stem: A study investigates the sources and effects of chemical pollutants in soil and water. Which branch is most relevant?
rationales: Correct: environmental chemistry studies chemical species and their sources, reactions, effects and fates in air, soil and water.
Analytical chemistry is concerned with analysing substances and their components.
Organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds, except for certain simple carbon salts.
Nuclear chemistry studies reactions and changes in atomic nuclei.

mcqs.stem: Which branch helps explain how physical laws affect atoms and molecules and can be used to predict reaction rates?
rationales: Correct: physical chemistry explains behaviour at atomic and molecular levels and helps predict and change reaction rates.
Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms.
Geochemistry studies Earth’s chemical composition, sources and minerals.
Medicinal chemistry focuses on discovering and developing medicines or drugs.

mcqs.stem: Which branch studies chemical substances and vital processes occurring in living organisms?
rationales: Correct: this is the study described for biochemistry.
Astrochemistry studies molecules and ions in space and their interactions with radiation.
Inorganic chemistry studies elements and compounds containing little or no carbon.
Polymer chemistry studies the properties, structure and synthesis of polymers and macromolecules.

mcqs.stem: A researcher studies the abundance and reactions of molecules and ions in interstellar space. Which branch is involved?
rationales: Correct: astrochemistry studies molecules and ions recurring in space and interstellar space.
Geochemistry studies the chemical composition of Earth and its sources and minerals.
Environmental chemistry focuses on chemical phenomena in the planet’s air, soil and water.
Analytical chemistry deals with analysis, separation, identification and concentration of components in substances.

mcqs.stem: Which branch focuses on the structure, properties and synthesis of large molecules made by linking building blocks?
rationales: Correct: polymer chemistry focuses on polymers and macromolecules.
Medicinal chemistry is concerned with designing, synthesizing and developing medicines.
Physical chemistry investigates behaviour at atomic and molecular levels and the physical laws involved.
Nuclear chemistry deals with reactions and transformations in atomic nuclei.

written.text: Q1.1. Why is there a need to divide Chemistry into many branches? Give three reasons.
written.finalAnswer: Chemistry is a widely spread and complex subject. Its branches allow scientists to concentrate on specific aspects. This focus helps scientists achieve breakthroughs and advancements.

rubric.why: Recognising the complexity of chemistry explains why one broad approach is not enough.
rubric.description: States that chemistry is widely spread or complex.
rubric.how: Mention that chemistry is a widely spread and complex subject.

rubric.why: The branches let scientists focus on particular aspects.
rubric.description: Explains that branches concentrate study on specific aspects.
rubric.how: State that each branch provides a focus on a specific area.

rubric.why: Focused study supports progress in the subject.
rubric.description: Mentions breakthroughs or advancements.
rubric.how: Explain that focused work helps scientists make breakthroughs or advancements.

rubric.why: The final point completes the reason for dividing the subject.
rubric.description: Gives the final reason: progress in chemistry.
rubric.how: Link the focused branches to scientific advancement.

modelAnswer: Chemistry is a widely spread and complex subject.
Its branches allow scientists to concentrate on specific aspects.
This focus helps scientists achieve breakthroughs and advancements.

written.text: Q1.2. Reactions may take place due to electrons present outside the nucleus or they may take place inside the nucleus. Which branches of Chemistry cover these two types of reactions?
written.finalAnswer: Reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are studied in the chemical branches, such as organic and inorganic chemistry; reactions taking place inside the nucleus are studied in nuclear chemistry.

rubric.why: The answer must identify branches dealing with ordinary chemical reactions involving electrons.
rubric.description: Names organic and/or inorganic chemistry for reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus.
rubric.how: Name the chemical branches, for example organic and inorganic chemistry.

rubric.why: Reactions inside the nucleus belong to a distinct branch.
rubric.description: Names nuclear chemistry for reactions inside the nucleus.
rubric.how: State that nuclear chemistry studies reactions in the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are studied in the chemical branches, such as organic and inorganic chemistry.
Reactions taking place inside the nucleus are studied in nuclear chemistry.

written.text: Q1.3. What types of problems are solved in analytical chemistry?
written.finalAnswer: Analytical chemistry solves problems involving the separation, identification and determination of the concentration of components present in material things.

rubric.why: Separation and identification are central kinds of analysis.
rubric.description: Mentions separation and identification of substances or components.
rubric.how: State that analytical chemistry separates and identifies components.

rubric.why: Determining how much of a component is present completes the definition.
rubric.description: Mentions determining the concentration of components.
rubric.how: State that it determines component concentrations.

modelAnswer: Analytical chemistry involves the separation and identification of components present in material things.
It also determines the concentration of these components.

written.text: Q1.3. Most of the molecules we study in biochemistry are organic in nature. Where does the difference exist in organic and biochemistry branches of Chemistry?
written.finalAnswer: Organic chemistry studies the structure, formation, properties, composition and reactions of carbon-containing compounds. Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms, including the structure and function of biological molecules.

rubric.why: The subject of organic chemistry must be identified.
rubric.description: States that organic chemistry studies carbon-containing compounds.
rubric.how: Name carbon compounds as the focus of organic chemistry.

rubric.why: These are among the aspects of carbon compounds studied in organic chemistry.
rubric.description: Gives aspects such as structure, properties, composition or reactions.
rubric.how: Mention one or more aspects of carbon compounds studied in organic chemistry.

rubric.why: Biochemistry is defined by its connection to living organisms and their processes.
rubric.description: States that biochemistry studies chemical substances or vital processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Name living organisms and their chemical processes.

rubric.why: The distinction is that biochemistry focuses on chemistry in living systems, even though many of its molecules are organic.
rubric.description: Clearly contrasts the scope of biochemistry with organic chemistry.
rubric.how: Explain that biochemistry focuses on chemical substances and processes in life.

modelAnswer: Organic chemistry studies the structure, formation, properties, composition and reactions of carbon-containing compounds.
Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes occurring in living organisms.
Thus, organic chemistry focuses on carbon compounds, while biochemistry focuses on chemical processes in living things.

written.text:
Q1.1. Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics.

(a) Rate of a reaction
(b) Digestion of food in human body
(c) Properties of plasma
(d) Ecosystem
(e) Reactions taking place during fireworks
(f) Measurement of the absorption of wavelength with the help of ultraviolet spectrometer
written.finalAnswer: (a) Physical chemistry (b) Biochemistry (c) Physical chemistry (d) Environmental chemistry (e) Inorganic chemistry (f) Analytical chemistry

rubric.why: Reaction rates are studied in physical chemistry.
rubric.description: Correctly names physical chemistry for the rate of a reaction and properties of plasma.
rubric.how: Identify physical chemistry for the rate and plasma properties.

rubric.why: Digestion is a chemical process in a living organism.
rubric.description: Names biochemistry for digestion.
rubric.how: Match digestion in the human body with biochemistry.

rubric.why: An ecosystem is an environmental topic.
rubric.description: Names environmental chemistry for an ecosystem.
rubric.how: Match the ecosystem with environmental chemistry.

rubric.why: Firework reactions and instrument-based measurement must be matched to their relevant branches.
rubric.description: Names inorganic chemistry for fireworks and analytical chemistry for ultraviolet spectrometer measurement.
rubric.how: Use inorganic chemistry for the reactions and analytical chemistry for measuring absorption.

modelAnswer: (a) Rate of a reaction — Physical chemistry
(b) Digestion of food in human body — Biochemistry
(e) Reactions taking place during fireworks — Inorganic chemistry
(f) Measurement of the absorption of wavelength with the help of ultraviolet spectrometer — Analytical chemistry

written.text: Q1.6. Differentiate between the areas which are studied under inorganic and organic chemistry.
written.finalAnswer: Inorganic chemistry studies the synthesis, composition, properties and structure of elements and compounds that contain little or no carbon. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives), other than simple salts such as carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides.

rubric.why: This is the key distinction in the textbook definition of inorganic chemistry.
rubric.description: Defines inorganic chemistry by compounds containing little or no carbon.
rubric.how: State the little-or-no-carbon distinction.

rubric.why: The definition also describes what is studied about inorganic substances.
rubric.description: Mentions aspects studied in inorganic chemistry, such as synthesis, composition, properties or structure.
rubric.how: Give at least one area studied for inorganic substances.

rubric.why: Carbon compounds are the central subject of organic chemistry.
rubric.description: Defines organic chemistry as the study of carbon compounds.
rubric.how: Name carbon compounds, hydrocarbons or their derivatives.

rubric.why: The simple carbon salts are an important stated exception.
rubric.description: Includes the exclusion of simple carbon salts, with suitable examples.
rubric.how: Mention that simple salts such as carbonates and bicarbonates are excluded.

modelAnswer: Inorganic chemistry studies the synthesis, composition, properties and structure of elements and compounds that contain little or no carbon.
Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, including hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
Simple carbon salts such as carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides are excluded from organic chemistry.

examTips: Board questions commonly ask you to match a topic or experiment with the correct branch of chemistry.

For a short-answer question about why chemistry is divided into branches, give separate points: the subject is complex, branches focus on specific areas, and this focus supports breakthroughs and advancements.
For a branch-definition question, state both what is studied and its distinctive focus; for example, analytical chemistry includes separation, identification and determining component concentrations.
For a comparison, define both branches clearly and include the stated exception for simple carbon salts in organic chemistry.

hints: Think about what the experiment is trying to find out.
Analytical chemistry analyses substances and determines their components.
yourTurn.question:
A lunar mission has recently brought samples from the Moon. The following experiments were then carried out on it. Point out the branch of chemistry these experiments are related to.

Experiment: Determining its composition
solution: The experiment determines the composition of a sample.
The branch that analyses substances and determines their components is analytical chemistry.

hints: The experiment studies what the materials are like, not what they are made of.
Physical chemistry investigates the behaviour and properties of substances.
yourTurn.question:
A lunar mission has recently brought samples from the Moon. The following experiments were then carried out on it. Point out the branch of chemistry these experiments are related to.

Experiment: Studying the physical properties of materials it contains
solution: The experiment studies physical properties of the materials.
The branch that investigates how substances behave and their physical properties is physical chemistry.

steps.why: The experiment asks for the branch that identifies what the lunar sample contains.
steps.text: Experiment 1: Determining its composition — analytical chemistry.

steps.why: The experiment concerns physical characteristics rather than composition or chemical reactions.
steps.text: Experiment 2: Studying the physical properties of materials it contains — physical chemistry.

steps.why: Using inorganic reagents to carry out reactions concerns inorganic substances and their reactions.
steps.text: Experiment 3: Carrying out chemical reactions with usual inorganic reagents — inorganic chemistry.

example.question:
A lunar mission has recently brought samples from the Moon. The following experiments were then carried out on it. Point out the branch of chemistry these experiments are related to.

1. Determining its composition
2. Studying the physical properties of materials it contains
3. Carrying out chemical reactions with usual inorganic reagents
example.answer:
1. Analytical chemistry
2. Physical chemistry
3. Inorganic chemistry

explain.title: What chemistry studies
explain.body: Chemistry studies substances: their properties, composition and structure. It also studies physical and chemical changes in matter and the laws or principles governing those changes. Composition means which elements and compounds are present and their percentages; structure means how atoms are arranged.

explain.title: Why chemistry has branches
explain.body: Chemistry is a widely spread, complex subject. Dividing it into branches allows scientists to focus on specific aspects and work towards breakthroughs and advancements.

explain.title: Recognise branches by their focus
explain.body: Physical chemistry studies behaviour at atomic and molecular levels. Analytical chemistry analyses substances and their components. Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms. Nuclear chemistry studies reactions in the nucleus.

explain.title: More branch clues
explain.body: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, with certain simple carbon salts excluded. Inorganic chemistry studies elements and compounds containing little or no carbon. Environmental chemistry studies chemical phenomena in the planet; medicinal chemistry deals with medicines; polymer chemistry with polymers; geochemistry with Earth’s chemical composition; and astrochemistry with molecules and ions in space.

mistakes: Do not confuse analytical chemistry, which analyses components and concentrations, with physical chemistry, which studies behaviour and physical laws.
Do not say organic chemistry studies every carbon-containing substance: the textbook excludes simple salts such as carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides.
Do not confuse biochemistry with organic chemistry: biochemistry focuses on chemical substances and processes in living organisms.
Do not choose nuclear chemistry for reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus; nuclear chemistry concerns reactions and transformations in the nucleus.
